That's the natural place: the silent app makes the grant, so it should tell the face at the same moment, with no waiting for a page to open. The one thing in the way: the silent app runs INSIDE the node, and the api the node hands it has no owner.command. It has post, but post can't make the owner's command signature. So there are two ways, and it's your pick:
(A) IN THE SILENT APP. The face is updated the moment a name is granted or freed. Cost: the silent app's api gets one call, command(to, verb, body). It's owner.command, unchanged, reached from inside the node: the call I asked about before.
(B) IN A SHELL APP. No new call. Cost: the face is updated only while that page is open.
I'd pick (A) now that you've pointed at the silent app: it's owner.command, not a new capability, and grants happen when no page is open. Say A or B.
taking public-app-server/G17 (why is the negotiator in the core; why nothing in the jobs monitor)
taking public-app-server/G17 -- Andy's '#1 why is the negotiator inside the core, not a silent app? why doesn't this show in the jobs monitor' (checking the tree).

Yours (18:24:53 beats my 18:24:55). Facts:
(1) THE NEGOTIATOR IS ALREADY AN APP. Grants, decide() and route answers live in app/appFaceApp, a booted, faceless app. What IS in core: puppetPost (the face's listener), appServers.js (starting app servers, toLocalApp), jobs.startServerJob. Worth saying which of these he means.
(2) JOBS. App servers ARE jobs: kind 'server', type 'app-server:<app>' (appServers.js startAll -> jobs.startServerJob), so they should appear in the jobs app. But the jobs app offers Cancel only for kind 'process' (app/jobs/jobs.js:47), so a server job can't be stopped from it. appFaceApp's happenings (grants, route answers, budget spent, hop failures) go to api.log, i.e. the node's console (nodeApps.js:406), NOT to any job. So nothing of the face's traffic is in the jobs monitor. A permanent job for appFaceApp (like fs-watcher, server-stats) would be where its log lines land.
Mine: my claim went out at 18:25:00, and yours arrived after it.

#1 It ISN'T in the core. appFaceApp is a faceless app, app/appFaceApp, with no page. But the node loads it INTO ITS OWN PROCESS ('boots': true, nodeApps.mountAll), and an app living there gets only the small api the node hands it. It has no loopback door, so no owner.command. A shell app talks to the node through the door and has everything. That in-process mounting is the whole reason for the question.
The clean fix follows from your point: RUN FACELESS APPS AS THEIR OWN PROCESSES, as 'server' jobs, the kind we built today for app servers. Such a process reaches the node through its loopback door like any shell app: owner.command, contacts, everything, with no new api.
#2 NOTHING SHOWS in the jobs monitor because a booted app isn't a job today. Its api.log goes to the console and nowhere else. As its own process it would be a job, and its output would land in the job's log. The app servers already work that way (jobs.startServerJob keeps their output).
RECOMMENDED: faceless apps become processes under the job system. That's a design row of its own (it touches how booted apps are loaded, which is core), and the member sync waits for it. Go! = I write that row.
taking public-app-server/G17 (why don't processes get a spirit object)

Yours. Fact for 'why don't those processes get a spirit object': today a spawned 'process' job gets two environment variables and nothing else, SPIRIT_JOB_ID and SPIRIT_CALLBACK_URL (the node's loopback door) (jobs.js:205-210). No library hands them interfaces, and no file under spirit/run/process/js reads SPIRIT_CALLBACK_URL. A 'server' job (startServerJob) gets NEITHER, only the IPC channel. So there's no spirit object for processes at all yet; booted apps are the only ones handed an api (nodeApps).

CORRECTION to my last: there IS a spirit object for process jobs. A process requires the kernel and gets spirit.core.jobs, whose report() reads SPIRIT_JOB_ID and SPIRIT_CALLBACK_URL (kernel.js:549-603: log lines, completed, failed). imageStats, wordpressScanner, lmStudio* and others use it. What still stands: a 'server' job (startServerJob) is spawned WITHOUT those two variables (only the IPC channel), so an app server can't report to its job even through that object. And the object hands jobs reporting only, not the rest of the api.

Honest answer: HALF of one exists. A process job loads kernel.js and gets the spirit object, but in a process only spirit.core.jobs works (report, log, complete, fail), through the address the node hands it (SPIRIT_CALLBACK_URL; kernel.js:568). The general door, spirit.core.ask, calls fetch('/api/spirit') (kernel.js:647). That only works in a browser page, which knows its own host; in a process it fails. And a 'server' job, the kind I built today, isn't given that address at all (wsl-claude caught that).
So your question is the design: the node hands every process it starts a spirit object that reaches the door, i.e. spirit.core.ask aimed at SPIRIT_CALLBACK_URL when there's no page. Then a faceless app run as a process has every verb a shell app has, owner.command included, and logs to its job. It's a small change, in kernel.js and startServerJob, and it's core. Go! = I write it up as the design row, with the member sync on top.
